decisions: EVERY NUMBER READS A VIEW. The rebuild happened because the old page summed trips.rate_sar in TypeScript and rendered 0 while Reports rendered 70,650 - rate_sar is NULL on all 676 rows.

DELIVERED REVENUE IS DASHBOARD-ONLY AND IS NEVER BILLED REVENUE. Reports, v_revenue_monthly and v_pnl_monthly are untouched and remain the only revenue the P&L knows. The two differ by TIMING (delivered now, invoiced later) and COVERAGE (delivered work never invoiced); billed can also EXCEED delivered when an invoice covers earlier periods and special charges. Never add them, never feed delivered into a margin, never label it plain 'Revenue'.

delivered_at IS NOT THE DAY THE WORK HAPPENED. It records when the stage button was pressed, and this fleet advances trips on the Kanban in bulk - 310 trips stamped on one afternoon, 22 distinct days against 35 by trip_date. 0109 buckets by trips.trip_date, which is also the Kanban's own day filter and v_delivery_output_daily's bucket, so those now agree by construction.

A full daily P&L is NOT POSSIBLE. Payroll has no daily source and was 98.9/67.3/74.9 percent of operating cost in Jun/Jul/Aug, so 0104 measures direct_cost_sar only and never calls it cost. Never label direct_margin as profit.
Delivery Output's bars are capacity DISPATCHED, a proxy. trips.tank_size_m3 is empty on every trip, so a real volume chart would be a flat zero line pretending to be a measurement.

An unpriceable trip is COUNTED, never guessed. One delivered trip has no project and so no rate: it contributes 0 and is counted in delivered_trips_unpriced, and the UI qualifies the figure only in months that actually have one.

Driver state may have EXACTLY TWO expressions: lib/driver-state.ts and v_driver_state_now. 0103 had embedded a second copy inside v_fleet_state_now; a drivers board would have made a third. The other views compose on it and a drift check asserts the two agree.

active means ASSIGNED (truck + live project), NOT currently driving. Three drivers hold in-flight trips with no assigned truck, so state and trip stage are separate columns and the contradiction is surfaced rather than resolved.
Compliance is four-valued. not_recorded never collapses into ok - five of eleven live drivers have no iqama_expiry and a missing date is not a passing check.
The projects month filter belongs in the LEFT JOIN, never WHERE. Measured on a quiet month: JOIN 6 rows, WHERE 0 rows - the WHERE form blanks every card and reads as an outage.
invoice_unpaid composes on v_receivables_open rather than restating its predicate. The restated version read 5 where Reports read 2. Do not simplify it back.
A failed read may never claim an empty queue. Shipped and fixed: the page rendered 'Every queue is clear right now' while the fetch had errored.
The hero spacer in DashboardClient.tsx is load-bearing - it is the search-bar intro, not decoration. Removing it removes the feature.

COMPONENTS/CHARTS.TSX IS DASHBOARD-ONLY and exactly one file imports it (app/DashboardClient.tsx, taking ComboChart and PieChart). app/reports and app/trips import BarChart/PieChart/ComposedChart from RECHARTS and app/consumption defines its own local ComboChart - a name grep finds those lookalikes and wrongly reports the ports as live. Check real import sites, not names.

BYTE-COMPARING .next/app-path-routes-manifest.json IS NOT A VALID IDENTITY TEST. Next emits it with non-deterministic key order - rebuilding one unchanged tree twice produces byte-different files. Parse it and compare the route set and mappings instead.

noUnusedLocals + noUnusedParameters are ON as of 6506f2e. A parameter genuinely required by a signature, interface or callback shape gets an _ prefix; it is never deleted, because that changes the shape the caller depends on.

context_notes: READ CLAUDE.md SECTION 7 FIRST - it is the durable record and this file is only a pointer to it. Working tree clean, 0 ahead / 0 behind origin/main at 3819188. FOUR THINGS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. (1) THE DELIVERED-REVENUE MISSTEP IS ON RECORD ON PURPOSE: 0108 bucketed by delivered_at and 0109 corrected it to trip_date; both are committed (f27229b, ad2b6e0) rather than squashed, same precedent as 0038 and 0090. Turki caught it from the chart shape alone - revenue on three days, zero on the rest - which is why the fix was to investigate the bucket rather than restyle the line. (2) THE DRIFT GUARD'S SHAPE IS THE LESSON: the first one lived behind a throwaway /dash-drift route, became unreachable when that route was deleted at teardown, and was deleted with it. The replacement runs on the Dashboard itself, renders nothing when healthy, and tracks reachable separately from ok because with no session RLS returns zero rows on BOTH sides and a naive comparison would score that as agreement. Do not move it back behind a diagnostic route. (3) CANVAS TEXT IS INVISIBLE TEXT - Chart.js paints its legend onto the canvas, so series names are pixels; ComboChart carries an aria-label and BarChart gained an optional one. Chart.js is a module import, so page.evaluate CANNOT reach Chart.getChart to read plotted values - numeric assertions belong in the migration verification blocks, not in Playwright, and the delivered-revenue spec says so where a reader would otherwise assume missing coverage. Three test bugs came from this area: an unscoped getByRole('alert') is never 0 in dev (Next mounts its own empty alert root outside the page tree), a negative assertion filtered div by text and took .first() so it silently resolved to the whole page wrapper, and a KPI selector expected 'REVENUE' when the uppercase is CSS-only. A negative assertion on an unscoped locator proves nothing. (4) SPEC FILES THAT CONTRADICT SHIPPED DESIGN GET DELETED, NOT LEFT TO FAIL: tests/dashboard-0108.spec.ts asserted an 'Invoiced revenue' series that was later dropped at Turki's call, so it was replaced by tests/dashboard-delivered-revenue.spec.ts - a spec asserting the opposite of intent is worse than no spec, because someone eventually fixes the code to match it. All tests/dashboard-*.spec.ts depend on deleted throwaway routes; they document what was verified, same convention as the reports and inventory specs. (5) DEAD-CODE HYGIENE IS NOW ENFORCED BY THE COMPILER, not by periodic sweeps: tsconfig carries noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters as of 6506f2e, flipped only AFTER the ten findings they would have flagged were cleared, so the flip itself was green. Two instruments were wrong the first time and both are worth not repeating - a name grep reported three genuinely dead chart ports as live because Reports/Trips import same-named components from recharts, and a byte-compare of the Next route manifest 'failed' because that file's key order is non-deterministic across builds of an unchanged tree. Verify by real import sites and by parsed route sets respectively.
